observations.trace: Preparation tickets carry typed owner and nonzero sequence; begin increments the global sequence with checked arithmetic, clones the owner active products into staged and resets facade/placement bindings, and current-ticket checks guard staged access and finish. Cancel clears matching staged/completed state; activate requires a matching completed ticket and input identity. Worker receive verifies each job/product variant and matching payload before staging.
observations.remaining: All callers, concurrent browser ordering, retention and supported failure semantics remain open; no worker or ticket sequence ran.

observations.trace: PreparedCityProduct stores document and graphics text; jobs checks both via matches and emits a regional-city job when either differs. The job generator parses graphics and uses its vista maximum_lods for prepared ground. begin retains the previous regional product in cloned staged state because begin_generation clears only facades and placements. finish_city and activate_city carry only ticket plus document, and the finish predicate tests staged city.document alone. Thus, if a same-document prior product exists and a request for changed graphics is finished without delivering the emitted regional-city job, source permits the prior product to satisfy completion; map admission activates that product by document.
observations.remaining: This is a conditional API-sequencing and ownership question, not an observed stale city. The actual browser prepareRegionalCity calls discover with runtime graphics, awaits run(jobs), checks abort, then finishes; the pool awaits all job work, receives each result, and rejects failures, and the request controller serializes preparations. Runtime graphics changes, untrusted/out-of-order callers, receiver and cache semantics, product policy and exact alias remain unproved. Preserve the normal all-jobs safeguard and existing resident reuse.

observations.trace: PreparedStrategicScene reconstructs occupied buildings only from staged placement/venue recipes, checks primary placements match input, checks promoted distant placement equivalence, requires a matching venue, and rejects any missing primary. Venue generation rejects a supplied recipe with a different program. An optional shell fast path and absent sign are explicit source modes.
observations.remaining: All admitted worker products, serialized data validation, omitted promoted-place policy and exact construction identities are not proven. No arbitrary payload or runtime failure is assumed.
